reconcile.connective: Gill's general explanation for gaps between the two registers — attrition, late joiners, copying slips — covers this ten-person shortfall too.

discrepancy.connective: Steve Wells presses this exact pairing as a contradiction: the same combined family returns 652 in Ezra and 642 in Nehemiah.

skeptic.name: Steve Wells
skeptic.attribution: Steve Wells, Skeptic's Annotated Bible (1999), contra/delaiah.html

excerpts.excerpt_text: …with some little difference of numbers and names; in some instances there are more in this list, in others fewer, which may be thus accounted for; that list was made in Babylon, when, upon the edict of Cyrus, the Jews, who intended to go up with Zerubbabel, gave in their names, and they were registered; but this was made when they came to Jerusalem; now some of those that gave in their names changed their minds, and tarried in Babylon, and some might die by the way, which makes the numbers fewer in some instances; and others who did not give in their names at first, but, being better disposed towards their own country, followed after and joined those which were returning, and increased the number of others …
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Gill's general account of why the Babylon-departure roll (Ezra 2) and the Jerusalem-arrival roll (Nehemiah 7) diverge numerically — people who changed their minds and stayed in Babylon, died en route, or joined late — is the standing harmonization for every clan-total gap in the shared list, including the Delaiah/Tobiah/Nekoda entry's 652-vs-642 discrepancy at Ezra 2:60 / Nehemiah 7:62.

pd_work.resource: John Haley, An Examination of the Alleged Discrepancies of the Bible (1874)
pd_work.author: John Haley
pd_work.note: Haley names the neighboring Arah variant explicitly (Ezra 2:5's 775 vs. Neh. 7:10's 652), then extends the same copyists'-blunder verdict as a blanket statement: "The other cases, some twenty in number, which appear from a comparison of Ezra ii. 6-60, with Neh. vii. 11-67, are to be explained in the same manner." That stated range ("Ezra ii. 6-60") explicitly reaches the Delaiah/Tobiah/Nekoda entry at Ezra 2:60, though Haley does not single it out by name.
